claim: Keepa provides Amazon price history charts and price drop alerts.
evidence: We provide Amazon price history charts and price drop alerts.

claim: Keepa's site lists price watches, daily drops and browser extensions among its features.
evidence: Amazon price history charts, price drop alerts, price watches, daily drops and browser extensions.

claim: The Keepa API delivers Keepa's data on Amazon marketplaces to the subscriber's own application.
evidence: The Keepa API delivers Keepa's data on Amazon marketplaces straight to your application.

claim: Keepa's API documentation lists 11 Amazon locales: com, co.uk, de, fr, co.jp, ca, it, es, in, com.mx and com.br.
evidence: 1 com 2 co.uk 3 de 4 fr 5 co.jp 6 ca 8 it 9 es 10 in 11 com.mx 12 com.br

claim: A Keepa Product Request retrieves up to 100 products per request at a base cost of 1 token per product.
evidence: Retrieves the product object for one or more products (up to 100 per request) ... The base cost is 1 token per product.

claim: Offer data includes New and Used Buy Box information with a history of Buy Box winners; requesting offers costs 6 tokens for every found offer page (up to 10 offers) per product, replacing the 1-token base cost.
evidence: 6 for every found offer page (contains up to 10 offers) per product ... Information on the New and Used Buy Box, including a history of Buy Box winners
verifier_note: Source says offer pages hold up to 10 offers and that with offers the basic 1-token-per-product charge does not apply; table row corrected and worked example recomputed (300 x 6 = 1,800, not 300 x (1+6) = 2,100).

claim: Product statistics give quick access to current prices, min/max prices and weighted mean values.
evidence: with quick access to current prices, min/max prices, and weighted mean values

claim: Keepa API access is limited by a token bucket, and plans differ by the number of tokens generated per minute.
evidence: Access to the API is limited via the token bucket algorithm. The plans differentiate by the number of tokens that are generated per minute.

claim: Unused API tokens expire after 60 minutes, so the 60-tokens-per-minute plan has a bucket capacity of 3,600 tokens.
evidence: Unused tokens expire after 60 minutes ... so the token bucket capacity is 3,600 tokens.

claim: Keepa's API plans are billed monthly in advance and continue from one billing period to the next until canceled.
evidence: Keepa's API plans are all billed monthly in advance and continue from one billing period to the next until canceled.

claim: An upgrade is charged immediately on a prorated basis; a downgrade gives a credit to the Keepa account, with no refund possible.
evidence: charged a prorated amount in case of an upgrade, or receive a credit to your Keepa account in case of a downgrade (no refund possible).

claim: A Keepa API subscription can be canceled at any time through the dashboard and terminates at the end of its period.
evidence: A subscription can be canceled at any time through your dashboard. Once canceled, it is scheduled to be terminated at the end of its period.

claim: Keepa accepts credit card payments through Stripe.
evidence: Keepa accepts payments via credit card through the payment provider Stripe.com.

claim: Every Keepa API request requires the API access key.
evidence: Every request requires your API access key as a parameter (`key`).

claim: Keepa API requests are issued over HTTPS and responses are always JSON.
evidence: All requests are issued over HTTPS and must accept gzip encoding. ... The response is always in JSON format.

claim: Product Search costs 10 tokens per search for up to 20 results; Best Sellers costs 50 tokens per request.
evidence: 10 tokens per search (up to 20 results) ... 50 tokens per request

claim: Browsing Deals costs 5 tokens per request for up to 150 deals.
evidence: 5 tokens per request (up to 150 deals)

claim: Keepa's Tracking API tracks product changes and notifies via webhook push or API pull.
evidence: Let Keepa track product changes and notify you — via webhook push or API pull.

claim: Each tracked product reduces the token refill rate: 0.9 tokens per update per locale for regular tracking.
evidence: Each tracked product decreases your token refill rate. ... 0.9 tokens per update per locale tracked

claim: Amazon's Product Opportunity Explorer groups products into niches built from customer search terms and analyzes trends in pricing, reviews and returns.
evidence: grouping search terms based on the products customers view or purchase after searching. It also analyzes trends in pricing, reviews, and returns.

claim: Amazon lists the Professional selling account at $39.99 a month plus selling fees.
evidence: A Professional selling account is $39.99/month + selling fees.

claim: Amazon's Automate Pricing tool is described as increasing the chances of becoming the Featured Offer.
evidence: Increase your chances of becoming the Featured Offer and drive more sales.

claim: Keepa says it tracks over 7 billion Amazon products.
evidence: Keepa tracks over 7 billion Amazon products.

claim: Keepa does not offer discounts on API plans.
evidence: Keepa does not offer discounts.

claim: An API plan can be downgraded only once every 28 days.
evidence: A downgrade is possible as well, but only once every 28 days.

claim: Several API subscriptions can run at once, each active simultaneously and sharing the same payment method and API key.
evidence: All subscriptions will be active simultaneously ... they share the same payment method and API key.

claim: A canceled subscription can be resumed until its period ends; once it has expired it can no longer be reactivated.
evidence: Until then you can resume it from your dashboard, and billing continues as before. ... it can no longer be reactivated

claim: Product Finder costs 10 tokens plus 1 per 100 ASINs, and Seller Information costs 1 token per seller plus 9 for the storefront.
evidence: 10 + 1 per 100 ASINs ... 1 token per seller (+9 for storefront)

claim: On a Product Request, the stats, history, days and only-live-offers parameters carry no extra token cost.
evidence: no extra token cost.

claim: The buybox parameter costs 2 tokens per product, rating up to 1 extra token per product, and update 0 or 1 per product.
evidence: 2 per product ... up to 1 extra token per product. ... 0 or 1 per product.

claim: The update parameter forces a refresh if the product's last update is older than the number of hours given.
evidence: If the product's last update is older than update hours, force a refresh.

claim: When the token balance runs out, requests fail with HTTP 429 and the message that you are out of tokens.
evidence: You are out of tokens. ... Wait until your token bucket refills.

claim: Each response reports tokensLeft (tokens currently left) and tokensConsumed (tokens this request consumed).
evidence: How many tokens you currently have left. ... Number of tokens this request consumed.

claim: Keepa prices are integers in the Amazon locale's smallest currency unit, such as cents.
evidence: The price is an integer of the respective Amazon locale's smallest currency unit (e.g., euro cents or yen).

claim: In the product object's csv histories, index 0 (AMAZON) is the Amazon price history and index 1 (NEW) the marketplace New price history.
evidence: Amazon price history ... Marketplace New price history

claim: Index 3 (SALES) is the sales rank history; not every product has one, and variation items usually lack individual ranks.
evidence: Sales Rank history (not every product has a Sales Rank; variation items usually don't have individual sales ranks)

claim: Index 10 (NEW_FBA) is the price history of the lowest third-party New offer fulfilled by Amazon.
evidence: Price history of the lowest 3rd party (not including Amazon/Warehouse) New offer that is fulfilled by Amazon.

claim: Index 11 (COUNT_NEW) is the history of how many marketplace merchants sell the product as new.
evidence: New offer count history (= count of marketplace merchants selling the product as new)

claim: Index 18 (BUY_BOX_SHIPPING) is the New Buy Box price history including shipping costs.
evidence: The New buy box price history, including shipping costs.

claim: Index 16 (RATING) is the rating history as an integer from 0 to 50, where 45 means 4.5 stars.
evidence: The product's rating history (an integer from 0 to 50, e.g., 45 = 4.5 stars).

claim: The monthlySold field states how often the product was bought in the past month.
evidence: How often this product was bought in the past month.

claim: The fbaFees field holds the FBA pick & pack fee, and referralFeePercentage the referral fee percentage at the assumed selling price.
evidence: Object containing the FBA pick & pack fee ... The Amazon referral fee percentage at the assumed selling price.

claim: Keepa timestamps are in Keepa Time minutes; Unix milliseconds are (keepaTime + 21564000) × 60000.
The statistics object gives 30- and 90-day averages, out-of-stock percentages and counts of sales rank drops.
evidence: Contains the 30-day out-of-stock percentage ... The count of sales rank drops (from a high to a low value) within the last 30 days

claim: The statistics object indicates whether Amazon is the Buy Box seller and whether the Buy Box is fulfilled by Amazon.
evidence: Indicates if Amazon is the seller in the Buy Box. ... Indicates whether the Buy Box is fulfilled by Amazon.

claim: The stats interval can be set as a number of most-recent days or as an explicit date range.
evidence: either as the number of most-recent days, or as an explicit date range:

claim: For the NEW, USED, COLLECTIBLE and REFURBISHED series, entries before February 23, 2026 reflect the lowest listing price and later entries the lowest landing price (listing price + shipping).
evidence: before February 23, 2026, reflect the lowest listing price ... on or after February 23, 2026, reflect the lowest landing price (listing price + shipping)

claim: A price value of -1 means no offer was available in that interval, for example because the item was out of stock.
evidence: If no offer was available in the given interval (e.g., out of stock), the price has the value -1.
